e1cd23f3d000b64fc5b3536e5328c89fc10fc704.summary: This is an index page from the US government (CISA) that lists advisories and malware analysis reports on North Korean government cyber activity, which the US calls HIDDEN COBRA. The listed items are dated 2017 to 2019. The page itself gives only titles and dates, so it is an index rather than a threat report.

e1e88bfe3d6b5b483692d31f0518c4571bd542ee.summary: GReAT of Kaspersky Lab reports on Carbanak, a criminal campaign against mainly financial institutions, aimed at stealing money rather than data. Up to 100 targets were hit; losses per bank ran from $2.5 million to about $10 million, with possible totals of $1 billion. Attackers used spear phishing emails and a Carberp-based backdoor. Cash-out methods included remote ATM dispensing, SWIFT transfers and altered account databases. Infections were first detected in December 2013 and peaked in June 2014.

e1030f278cd33eba34a284c6ad0d5a350b1da9eb.summary: Blog post by independent macOS researcher Patrick Wardle (Objective-See, February 2021) on malware compiled natively for Apple silicon. It analyses GoSearch22, a Pirrit-linked adware app whose universal binary includes arm64 code. The app was signed with a developer ID in November 2020, and the certificate was later revoked. The post also describes anti-analysis behaviour, a Safari extension, and lower detection rates for the arm64 build.
